sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Pendleton County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for land in Pendleton County are recorded at the Pendleton County Clerk's office at 233 Main Street, Room 1, Falmouth, KY 41040. The mailing address is PO Box 112, the phone is 859-654-3380 and the fax is 859-654-5600. The clerk's website lists hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday and 8:30 a.m. to noon on the second and last Saturday of each month, except on holiday weekends.

Kentucky requires a deed to be recorded in the county where the land lies, as KRS 142.050 notes when it refers to KRS 382.110. A house near Butler or DeMossville therefore goes through the Falmouth office even if the seller lives in another state.

sections.h2: What is Pendleton County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Pendleton County covers about 280 square miles of northern Kentucky hills, roughly halfway between Cincinnati and Lexington. It was formed in 1798 from parts of Campbell and Bracken counties and is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area. Falmouth, the county seat, sits where the Main and South Licking rivers meet, and Butler, the other city, is on the Licking River about 10 miles north. The Ohio River forms the county's northeastern border with Ohio.

Falmouth began as a settlement called Forks of Licking around 1776 and was chartered in 1793. Butler grew up around 1852 when the Kentucky Central Railroad came through. Kincaid Lake State Park, with 850 acres for camping, golf, swimming and fishing, lies within the county.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Pendleton County homes?
sections.html:
The county is small and mostly owner-occupied, and many residents commute.

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 14,800, up 1.1 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home (2020 to 2024): $159,800.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 74.7 percent among 5,442 households.
  • Median household income: $64,669; median gross rent: $793.
  • Mean travel time to work: 36.4 minutes.
  • Housing units: 6,341, and no building permits recorded in 2025.

With rentals making up about a quarter of occupied homes and little new construction, most sales here involve existing houses, so the deed history matters.

sections.h2: How much does the Pendleton County Clerk charge to record documents?
sections.html:
The clerk's site lists flat fees by document type under KRS 64.012. The state transfer tax is collected separately and is not part of these figures.

Pendleton County Clerk recording fees (Pendleton County Clerk, Document Fees page)
DocumentFee
Deed$50
Deed with a release$96
Deed with a state fee exemption$46
Mortgage$80
Mortgage with assignment$126
Release$46
Affidavit of descent$50
Power of attorney$50
Plat$50
Judgment lien$46

A certified copy costs $5 and a regular copy costs $2. Ask the clerk for a single total before preparing the check, since a package of documents can mix several of these rates.

sections.h2: What must a Kentucky deed contain before the Pendleton County Clerk accepts it?
sections.html:
Under KRS 382.135, the clerk may not accept a deed that skips any of these items.

  • Full names and mailing addresses of the grantor and the grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration.
  • An in-care-of address where the property tax bill for the year of transfer can be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized statement from both sides that the stated price is the full price paid, or, for a gift, a sworn statement of the estimated fair cash value.

Deeds that only convey utility easements, government rights of way or cemetery lots, or that correct an earlier deed, are excused from the consideration, in-care-of and sworn-statement items.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies to a Pendleton County sale?
sections.html:
The grantor pays 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction, and the clerk must collect it before accepting the deed (KRS 142.050). The clerk keeps 5 percent as a collection fee and sends the rest to the county treasurer every three months. At the county median value of $159,800, the tax is $160.00, since the price spans 320 units of $500.

Exemptions include deeds that correct an earlier deed, deeds that secure or release a debt, transfers between spouses, transfers after foreclosure and transfers from parent to child for nominal consideration. For a gift, the tax is based on the market price the house would bring in an open sale.

sections.h2: How are inherited or encumbered houses handled at the Pendleton County Clerk?
sections.html:
When a house passes by will or intestate succession, the personal representative must file an affidavit with the clerk before closing out the estate, naming who received each property and its value (KRS 382.135(4)). The clerk's fee for an affidavit of descent is $50, and recording a will costs $46.

Liens are recorded in the same office. A certificate of delinquency costs $46 to record and $46 to release, and the Department of Revenue says unpaid property tax bills move from the sheriff to the county clerk after April 15, with a lien recorded against the property. Judgment liens and mechanics' liens each cost $46 to record and $46 to release. A seller should ask the clerk to run the parcel before listing it.

sections.h2: What should a Pendleton County seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
• Locate the book and page of the deed that put the property in your name.
  • Confirm whether any lien, lis pendens or certificate of delinquency is recorded against the parcel.
  • Decide the in-care-of address that goes in the new deed.
  • Arrange a notary, since the deed needs a sworn statement of consideration.
  • Ask the clerk for a total of recording fees and transfer tax so the closing statement is accurate.

Heirs with a vacant Pendleton County house who want to skip repairs can ask for a cash offer, and the buyer's closing agent then handles the same recording steps.

faqs.q: What are the Pendleton County Clerk's hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office also opens from 8:30 a.m. to noon on the second and last Saturday of each month, except on holiday weekends.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: The posted fee for a deed is $50. A deed that includes a release is $96, and a deed that is exempt from the state fee is $46.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I pay in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value or fraction. On a home worth $159,800 that is $160.00, and the clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does the Pendleton County Clerk record a power of attorney?
faqs.a: Yes. The posted fee is $50, and a power of attorney recorded together with a revocation costs $96.

faqs.q: Where do I get a certified copy of a recorded deed in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: At the Clerk's office in Falmouth. The clerk's fee list shows $5 for a certified copy and $2 for a regular copy.
